title: Dentistry - Mr Hunter

caseNotes: Patient is Mr William Hunter, DOB 04 December 1964, address 404 West Road, Newtown.
Medical background: Type 2 diabetes.
Attendance at doctor is irregular.
Blood pressure elevated at 150/95.
Medications: Metformin hydrochloride (Diabex) 500mg twice daily.
Medications: Captopril (Capoten) 25mg twice daily.
Social background: smoker, 25 cigarettes per day.
Poor diet.
Last dental visit was 2015, with 3 extractions.
Irregular dental attendance; patient does not like the dentist, since childhood.
Brushing is irregular (forgets to brush) and patient never flosses.
09 Aug 2019 extraoral exam: no cervical lymphadenopathy; incompetent lips.
Intraoral soft tissue exam: draining sinus adjacent to tooth 36, with no buccal swelling.
Saliva appears thin; mouth is dry.
Restorations present on teeth 11, 12, 16, 23, 26 and 44.
Periodontal Screening and Recording (PSR) score of 333/333.
Oral hygiene is poor.
Gross calculus deposits both supra- and sub-gingivally.
Gingivae bleed readily on probing with exudate from pockets.
Bitewing radiographs show caries on tooth 36 (DO), with no other carious lesions noted.
Generalised horizontal bone loss and vertical defects noted on radiographs.
Periapical radiograph of tooth 36 shows radiolucency associated with the distal root.
Percussion test on tooth 36 slightly tender, though not particularly painful.
Sensibility test negative to CO2 and electric pulp testing on tooth 36.
Palpation: no pain.
Diagnosis: pulpal necrosis with draining sinus associated with tooth 36 (disto-occlusal carious lesion).
Diagnosis: moderate to severe generalised periodontitis, to be confirmed after a full periodontal examination.
Diagnosis: poor oral hygiene.
Treatment plan: extraction or root canal treatment (RCT) of tooth 36.
Treatment plan: oral hygiene instruction with full-mouth scaling and root planing.
Treatment plan: smoking cessation.
30 Aug 2019: full periodontal chart completed, confirming the diagnosis, with gross supragingival calculus present full-mouth.
Patient consented to a blood sugar level (finger-prick) test; result was 20mmol/L (normal range 3.0-5.5mmol/L).
Patient does not want to see a periodontist.
Patient agreed to 4 quadrant scaling visits under local anaesthetic.
Patient has chosen extraction of tooth 36 at the next visit.
Patient last saw his doctor (Dr Wong, Newtown Medical Centre) for diabetes in February 2019.
Given the risks of extraction with the current blood sugar level, patient was advised to see his doctor to get his diabetes under control before the extraction.
Referral to the doctor is needed regarding poor diabetes control, smoking cessation, and the necessity for extraction of tooth 36 due to risk of further infection.
The extraction was completed without complications.
candidateLetter:
Dr Tanya Wong
Newtown Medical Centre
77 North Road
Newtown

30 August 2019

Dear Dr Wong,
Re: Mr William Hunter, DOB: 4 December 1964

I am writing to request further assessment and management of Mr William Hunter's blood glucose levels before extraction of tooth 36.

Mr Hunter attended today, when a full periodontal chart confirmed moderate to severe generalised periodontitis, with gross full-mouth supragingival calculus. His blood sugar level on finger-prick testing was 20 mmol/L, against a normal range of 3.0 to 5.5 mmol/L. He has chosen extraction at his next visit. Extraction should be deferred until his diabetes is better controlled, given the risk of further infection.

On 9 August 2019, Mr Hunter was found to have a draining sinus adjacent to tooth 36, with no buccal swelling. Radiographs showed a disto-occlusal carious lesion and radiolucency at the distal root, and the diagnosis was pulpal necrosis.

Mr Hunter has type two diabetes mellitus and takes metformin hydrochloride, 500 mg twice daily and captopril, 25 mg twice daily. His blood pressure was 150/95 mmHg. He last attended his doctor for diabetes in February 2019 and attends irregularly. He smokes twenty-five cigarettes per day and has a poor diet.

I would be grateful if you could also discuss smoking cessation with Mr Hunter.

Should there be any queries, kindly do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Dentist
